record.paper_title: Kontsevich Graphs Act on Nambu-Poisson Brackets, VI. Open Problems
record.original_question: What group-theoretic and topological mechanism makes Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations vanish as differential-polynomial formulas, especially in cases where a vanishing micro-graph has trivial automorphism group and no evident symmetry that marks the cancelling factors?

evidence.quote: What is the group-theoretic and topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs and their linear combinations ?
To reveal this mechanism in full is a standing problem; the impact of topology (in Γ) on arithmetic (in φ(Γ)) will make possible the study of d ≳ 5, so far costly.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix an integer d ≥ 3 and consider the Nambu–Poisson bracket on R^d given, with respect to a fixed volume/Casimir functions a_1,...,a_{d-2}, by the Jacobian determinant
  {f,g}_P = Jac(a_1,...,a_{d-2},f,g).
A "Nambu micro-graph" Γ is a finite oriented graph (in the Kontsevich graph calculus, refined so that each Poisson-bivector vertex is resolved into a subgraph encoding the Jacobian-determinant structure, with internal edges decorated by partial derivatives acting on the Casimirs a_i and on external arguments). To every such micro-graph Γ one associates a differential-polynomial expression φ(Γ) in the components of a_1,...,a_{d-2} and the external functions, obtained by the usual rule of contracting partial-derivative tensors along the edges and (anti)symmetrizing over the Jacobian indices.

Problem. Identify a group-theoretic and topological mechanism that explains the identical vanishing φ(Γ) ≡ 0 of Nambu micro-graphs Γ, and of their linear combinations Σ c_i Γ_i, as differential polynomials in (a_1,...,a_{d-2}) and the arguments. The mechanism is required to apply in particular to those cases in which a vanishing micro-graph has trivial automorphism group Aut(Γ) = {1} and exhibits no manifest combinatorial symmetry able to pair up and cancel the contributing monomial terms. More precisely: produce a structural criterion — formulated in terms of the underlying topology of Γ (vertex/edge incidences, cyclic structures, embeddings) together with the action of an explicit (sub)group on the index/Casimir data — that is both necessary and sufficient for φ(Γ) ≡ 0, and that reproduces the known list of vanishing 1-vector Nambu micro-graphs in dimension d = 3 while extending to d ≥ 4.
artifact.category_tag: Kontsevich graph calculus for Nambu–Poisson brackets
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is explicitly posed as a standing open question in the most recent installment (2025) of the series on Kontsevich graphs acting on Nambu–Poisson brackets. Companion papers (parts II, IV, V) identify partial instances (e.g., twelve vanishing 1-vector micro-graphs in d=3, and cases where non-trivial automorphism groups acting on Casimirs explain vanishing), but no general group-theoretic/topological mechanism covering trivial-automorphism cases is established. A 2025 student thesis at Groningen also frames this as an outstanding constraint problem. No published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, VI. Open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the group-theoretic/topological mechanism of vanishing for Nambu micro-graphs as a standing open problem, noting that revealing it would enable study in dimension d ≳ 5.
status_evidence.claim: The vanishing mechanism is explicitly stated as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich graphs act on Nambu–Poisson brackets, IV. When the invisible becomes crucial
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies invisible (vanishing-as-formula) micro-graphs in d=3 whose descendants need not vanish in d=4, motivating the search for a structural mechanism.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist but the general mechanism is not given.

status_evidence.title: Kontsevich (micro-)graph invariants in the geometry of Nambu-Poisson brackets: their nature and constraints
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses constraints and vanishing phenomena for Nambu micro-graphs, treating the topic as ongoing research.
status_evidence.claim: Independent recent work treats this as an unresolved question.
